children: The Reserve Bank of India’s September 15 deadline for payment aggregators to complete the re-KYC of existing merchants is proving to be a much more complicated exercise than simply collecting a few updated documents.
With less than a fortnight to go, more than a million online merchants and around 30 percent of the UPI QR merchants could potentially fail to furnish the required documentation before the deadline.

KYC, or know your customer verification, is a process done by financial institutions to confirm the identity and address of the user. This is important to trace any illegal activities such as fraud or money laundering.

The KYC backlog follows the RBI’s updated and consolidated Master Directions, issued in September 2025, which formally categorise payment aggregators into three segments: PA-Online, PA-Physical and PA-Cross Border.
RBI guidelines require PAs to undertake due diligence of merchants in line with its new standards, including checks on the nature of the business and the background and antecedents of the merchant.

The central bank also set a September 15, 2026 deadline for payment aggregators to complete full re-KYC verification of existing merchants, failing which their payments will be paused. For merchants onboarded on or after January 1, 2026, verification was required before they could accept payments.
Education and reaction

To be sure, the regulator’s master direction came late last year, and from merchants to payment aggregators, everyone had enough time to comply. However, the tendency of parking the process until the last minute could create payment disruptions.

For payment aggregators (PAs), the challenge is not only reaching millions of merchants across the country but also getting them to understand what is required under the RBI’s KYC and merchant due-diligence framework.
This becomes particularly difficult in the long tail of India’s merchant ecosystem, where many businesses are small, informal or run by individuals.

Such merchants often do not maintain the documentation that a formal business would typically have, and may not even be familiar with concepts such as beneficial ownership or the documentation required to establish it.
The process has disproportionately affected smaller merchants.

“This goes against the government’s and regulator’s financial inclusion agenda as the informal merchants are the ones struggling most with KYC verification,” said a senior executive with a payments firm.

The documentation burden can consequently include PAN details, incorporation documents, registered and operating addresses, information on directors and shareholders, tax returns and details of the company’s equity structure.
While most of these are not applicable for small businesses, similar details on ownership, addresses, PAN Cards have stumped most merchants.
Digital KYC is not enough
The RBI’s requirements also extend beyond paperwork. In specified cases, PAs have to conduct contact-point verification of merchants and physically verify information against original documents.
This means that a digital onboarding process can ultimately require a physical visit by a PA representative.

That has forced payment companies to build a sizeable on-ground verification network. Industry executives said PAs have had to rapidly expand their teams of employees who can conduct physical verification across cities, smaller towns and rural areas.
Another RBI mandate that requires such verification to be carried out by PA employees rather than being entirely outsourced to third-party agencies has added to the operational complexity.

For the merchant, meanwhile, the PA has increasingly become the de facto guide through the compliance process. Apart from collecting documents, payment companies have to explain what needs to be submitted, help merchants understand ownership and business verification requirements and follow up when documents are incomplete or inconsistent.
This has inundated and overwhelmed most PA firms, as Moneycontrol reported in the case of Google developers struggling with their KYC process.

title: How RBI’s re-KYC mandate has become a new headache for merchants and payment firms
